articles.title_orig: World News in Brief: Child migrants in Europe, Greenland forced contraception scandal, FAO hunger updates
articles.title_zh: World News in Brief: Child migrants in Europe, Greenland forced contraception scandal, FAO hunger updates
articles.content_orig:
Facebook Twitter Print Email
New data on child migrants published on Wednesday highlighted the harrowing treatment many face while travelling to Europe in search of work and shelter.
Just over 31,000 children arrived in Greece, Italy, Spain, Bulgaria and Malta last year – 25 per cent less than in 2024.
Of more than 4,600 teenagers and young adults aged 15 to 24 surveyed, nearly half reported suffering physical violence.
One of the main routes migrants take today is the through the central Mediterranean from Libya and Tunisia in northern Africa to Italy, according to the UN migration agency, IOM .
IOM spokesperson Kennedy Omondi said there has to be stronger cooperation between European countries and those along migration routes to protect children travelling alone.
“The latest data in our report shows how vulnerable children are subjected to violence and exploitation when safe pathways are limited and they are forced to rely on smugglers,” the spokesperson said.
Among the adolescents and young adults who made the journey, 28 per cent said they had been held against their will and 17 per cent said they had been forced into work. Almost eight in 10 are male.
One 19-year-old migrant worker from Bangladesh cited in the report said his boss in Libya took away his passport and forced him into slave labour, hitting him when he was considered not to be working hard enough.
A 20-year-old woman from Liberia said she arrived in Algeria where she was raped and forced to work as a cleaner. Seven months’ pregnant, she escaped on a boat to Spain.
Most cases of abuse occurred in Libya, according to IOM. More than 20,000 of the 31,100 children who reached Europe along mixed migration routes last year arrived without a parent or guardian, according to a joint report with the UN Children’s Fund ( UNICEF ) and refugee agency, UNHCR .
IOM Director General Amy Pope called for stronger cooperation between European countries and States along migration routes to protect children travelling alone. Ms. Pope also called for action to tackle the smuggling and criminal networks that exploit them.
Independent UN human rights experts have warned that attempts to downplay the forced contraception of thousands of Inuit women and girls in Greenland threaten any prospect of genuine redress.
The concerns follow a dissenting report by two former members of an expert group appointed by Greenland’s Government.
It concluded there were no empirical grounds to assume that Danish or Greenlandic authorities intentionally and systematically inserted intrauterine devices without consent.
The two governments have already recognised that the Indigenous women and girls endured the practice for decades in public care institutions and have apologised.
But, the independent experts – who receive no salary for their work and are not UN staff – said true remedy cannot be achieved without “a clear, accurate and undisputed record of historical facts”.
They urged Denmark to make compensation schemes more accessible linguistically and culturally, ensure women with disabilities are not forgotten and address wider abuses such as forced adoption and the removal of Inuit children from their parents.
“Their dignity, voices and rights must remain at the centre of all efforts toward truth, justice, healing and reconciliation,” the Human Rights Council -appointed experts said.
The UN Food and Agriculture Organization ( FAO ) has called for urgent funding to help families in the Near East and North Africa to keep growing food and earning a living as conflict, displacement and climate pressures deepen hunger.
More than 45 million people across the region face crisis-level hunger or worse.
At the same time, funding shortfalls are limiting support to protect food production.
In Sudan, where 19.5 million people face high levels of acute food insecurity, only 23 per cent of the $193 million needed under the 2026–2028 emergency response plan has been funded. In Yemen, FAO has secured less than one per cent of the $87.9 million it requires for 2027.
In Lebanon, more than one million people were displaced after the March 2026 escalation, and more than 22 per cent of agricultural land has reportedly been damaged.
“Investing early in seeds, livestock, water and other agricultural support can protect livelihoods, prevent hunger from deepening and reduce humanitarian needs over time,” said FAO Deputy Director-General Beth Bechdol.

articles.title_orig: How PvP Progression in World of Warcraft: Forever Works
articles.title_zh: How PvP Progression in World of Warcraft: Forever Works
articles.content_orig:
Whether you’re charging into battlegrounds with your faction or setting your sights on long-term PvP (Player vs. Player) goals, World of Warcraft: Forever brings a refreshed sense of purpose to every match-up. This approach gives players more reasons to take part throughout the season while preserving the spirit of competition that defined PvP in the original World of Warcraft .
When reimagining the PvP system, we wanted to keep the design pillar of “Approachable and Familiar” firmly in view: simplifying the original Honor System while staying true to its roots.
In World of Warcraft: Forever, PvP progression has two parts: Honor and Rank Points.
Honor is a currency players earn through taking part in PvP content. This includes defeating other players, completing battlegrounds, and finishing relevant PvP quests. Players also earn increased Honor in highlighted battlegrounds during their holiday weeks.
As part of these updates, we reviewed Honor gains across battlegrounds so acquisition rates are more consistent across the board. We want players to enjoy the full range of battleground maps without feeling compelled to choose Alterac Valley solely for Honor efficiency.
Rank Points come from PvP activities such as battlegrounds and relevant PvP quests, with holiday-week battlegrounds offering an additional boost. As players earn Rank Points, they advance through familiar PvP ranks from original World of Warcraft, working toward the ultimate titles of High Warlord for the Horde or Grand Marshal for the Alliance. Ranks have a weekly cap, retaining the foundation of the original system while making the journey more accessible.
Honor can be used to purchase two sets of PvP gear: one blue-quality set and one epic-quality set. The epic set requires the blue piece plus an Emboldened Seal to upgrade it, and Emboldened Seals have rank requirements players must reach before purchasing. There are also new and reworked items to fill gaps for specializations that were previously missing options. For example, Shaman now have healer, melee, and caster PvP gear sets they can acquire.
Below are the rank requirements for PvP item rewards:
Rank 1 - Tabard Rank 2 - PvP Trinket Rank 3 - Cloaks Rank 4 - Necklace Rank 5 - Combat Potions Rank 6 - Tabard Rank 7 - Battle Standard Rank 8 - Epic Bracers/Epic Belt Upgrade Token Rank 9 - Epic Boots Upgrade Token Rank 10 - Epic Gloves Upgrade Token Rank 11 - Mounts Rank 12 - Epic Legs/Epic Shoulders Upgrade Token Rank 13 - Epic Chest/Epic Helm Upgrade Token Rank 14 - Epic Weapons
To view your progress, you can open your Character Pane (Hotkey-C) then select the Player vs. Player tab on the right side of the interface. It will show you your rank, your current Rank Points, and what rewards are available for purchase based on your rank.
During a PvP season, players can progress through the ranks and earn Honor. Each season also includes a journey with weekly tasks to complete. Successfully completing those tasks grants Honor and Rank Points, and three tasks each season also grant a Legacy Point. Completing these tasks is part of the seasonal journey, and because they are tied to the Legacy System, they remain available to complete in future seasons.
With more ways to make progress each week and meaningful goals to pursue throughout the season, PvP in World of Warcraft: Forever gives players a clear path to jump in, compete, and keep building toward what comes next.

articles.title_orig: Reports of sexual violence are up. Data from Cornell and other colleges in 8 charts.
articles.title_zh: Reports of sexual violence are up. Data from Cornell and other colleges in 8 charts.
articles.content_orig:
Gang rape allegations at Cornell University are fueling a firestorm of actions against the school, against fraternity members named in a lawsuit and against the former student known as Jane Doe, whose accusations have galvanized a nationwide reckoning of sexual assault on college campuses .
Doe, who recently filed a lawsuit alleging gang rape at Cornell’s Chi Phi fraternity house in 2024, has now received death threats, her attorney Thomas Giuffra said. He provided CNN audio of one of the harassing calls.
Doe was also targeted in a swatting incident , during which police drew guns on her family and a friend, the attorney told CNN’s Jake Tapper.
“The temperature needs to be brought down,” Giuffra said, blaming the threats on commentators who have doxxed the woman and accused her of lying. “I am very concerned for her and her family’s safety.”
A timeline of the Cornell gang rape allegations
Meanwhile, some of the accused fraternity members – and even others who are unrelated to the case but have the same names – have faced public backlash as the investigation unfolds.
And Cornell, which recently announced a former Justice Department official will investigate the school’s handling of sexual assault claims, is the site of a seven-hour sit-in on campus to show “solidarity with Jane Doe,” according to flyers for the event.
Sexual assault survivor says Cornell Jane Doe is ‘not alone’, and laments lack of accountability
The state attorney general has launched a separate investigation as questions mount over how Cornell police handled Jane Doe’s allegations, how much information was shared with the district attorney’s office at the time, why prosecutors initially decided not to file charges , and whether the school’s internal investigation and actions went far enough.
Professors joined students at a rally this week, where demonstrators held signs reading “Justice for every Jane Doe” and “Cornell admin betrays survivors resign now.”
While Cornell’s president expressed his own anger about what happened with Jane Doe’s case, at least one faculty member is now calling for his resignation.
Students at sit-in hope for change: Students demonstrating at the university’s dining hall Wednesday said they are eager and hopeful for change. “I want to make it clear to the administration that us students aren’t OK with its response to this case,” Maggie Jacobsohn, a freshman, said. “Part of the sit-in is to make sure that we don’t continue with business as usual.” Hannah Gellert, another freshman, said she was supporting the greater cause. “It’s not just Cornell that is facing these horrible events. I think it’s really good that it’s being brought up into the media so it can be addressed on a larger scale,” she said. Students’ trust in the administration is “really low,” Cornell senior Madeline Gage told CNN’s Boris Sanchez Wednesday. “That trust only keeps declining as more details of this case are coming out,” Gage said.
Some accused students are still in school: University officials confirmed two students named in Doe’s civil lawsuit last month are still enrolled and attending classes, according to a recording of a virtual webinar obtained by CNN. Some faculty members said they’re struggling to teach classes the accused students are in and raised questions about how to accommodate them and other students.
Faculty member calls for president’s resignation: “There are layers of concerns that need to be addressed. And I think the only way to begin that process is to see resignations and a turnover in our upper administration,” Cornell Faculty Senate member Ariana Kim told CNN’s Wolf Blitzer on Wednesday morning. She specifically called for the resignation of Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff, who was interim president at the time of Doe’s allegations to campus police in 2024.
Doe’s attorney details more threats: Doe has been targeted with threats and attempts to publicize her identity, her attorney told CNN’s Anderson Cooper on Tuesday night. “Just before I got on with you, somebody called her, made a threat to shoot up her house, shoot her, her mother, her father. She’s calling the police as we speak now,” Giuffra told Cooper. While Doe has received other threats since filing her lawsuit, this was the first phone call, Giuffra said. “We’re terrified,” said the attorney, who previously said that he himself received a threat Sunday morning.
Jane Doe receives phone threat over Cornell case, attorney says
Mayor calls for a pause on student gatherings : The Ithaca Common Council is scheduled to meet at 6 p.m. Wednesday at City Hall as Mayor Robert Cantelmo seeks council action on a proposed moratorium on student and special event permits – including Greek life and other student gatherings – following the allegations of gang rape at Cornell’s Chi Phi fraternity house in 2024.
No-confidence vote coming: The Faculty Senate will review a resolution for a no-confidence vote before it’s added to the Senate’s meeting agenda for October 14, labor history professor and Faculty Senate member Paul Ortiz said. The Senate is Cornell’s main legislative advisory and review body, with more than 75 members representing the university’s faculty. So far, about 40 senators have supported a resolution to hold a vote of no confidence, Ortiz said. CNN has reached out to Cornell officials for comment.
Cornell says ex-US Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates will investigate school’s response to Jane Doe’s rape allegations
Students host town hall : Students on Tuesday also hosted a town hall to discuss the ongoing issues on campus. A young woman in attendance said the event had helped “restore my faith in the community.” Another student said they were glad to see the media spotlight being shined on the school. “Sexual violence should make the headlines. It should be shocking, it should be newsworthy because it should be incredibly rare,” they said.
Cornell announces independent review : Former US Deputy Attorney General Sally Q. Yates will lead an independent review of how Cornell University “prevents and responds to sexual harassment, sexual assault and related misconduct on campus,” the university announced Tuesday. Yates and her team will “conduct a detailed review of the university’s response” to Doe’s allegations, “including whether Cornell followed its policies and procedures in responding to the matter,” the university said.
The cycle of denial and shame felt by Cornell’s Jane Doe follows a typical pattern for sexual assault survivors, experts say
Sexual violence survivors reach out for help in near-record numbers : Over the past week, calls to the National Sexual Assault Hotline are up 73%, and there were more than double the normal number of calls on Monday alone, according to the Rape, Abuse and Incest National Network, which operates the hotline. Many of those contacting the hotline said reading about Doe’s case inspired them to call, RAINN President Scott Berkowitz said. “We admire – and are so grateful for – Jane Doe’s courage,” Berkowitz said. “RAINN stands with her, as do millions of survivors and supporters across the country.”
Cornell police tried to get phone records in Jane Doe’s sex assault investigation. Her lawyer says records never got to DA
Cornell police drafted requests to phone companies : Documents reveal Cornell police drafted letters to wireless carriers while “investigating a sexual assault incident” about a week after Doe first reported the alleged assault to university police. The drafts, addressed to Verizon and T-Mobile, asked them to “preserve all available data,” including texts, calls, and picture and video messages associated with accounts that “may contain evidence pertinent to the ongoing investigation.” It’s not clear whether investigators ever sent those requests or followed up with subpoenas. And it’s also unclear whether Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten was aware of the 2024 draft letters. The DA has said Cornell police only gave his off

articles.title_zh: Microsoft Surface and Windows Event 2026: All the Announcements and Analysis Live From San Francisco
articles.content_orig:
Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...
SAN FRANCISCO—In what is sure to be a jam-packed presentation, Microsoft finally seems ready to talk more about its Nvidia RTX Spark-powered Surface Laptop Ultra , along with its visions for Copilot and Windows . Between Computex and Build earlier this year, it's clear that Redmond has been cooking up some fresh ( and likely expensive ) ideas about personal computing in the age of AI and agents , and we can't wait to hear more.
Whatever Microsoft reveals at its surprise fall event, which starts on Wednesday, Oct. 7, at 10 a.m. PT (1 p.m. EST), we'll be covering it all live. Make sure to tune in early and check back often, though, as we'll be updating this story with from-the-ground insights and deeper analysis throughout the week. You can also watch the event live from the Windows YouTube channel, starting at 12:45 EST.
The announcement of this event was somewhat unexpected, so no one knows for sure what to expect. That said, we're pretty confident that it will include plenty of news about RTX Spark PCs (including the Surface Laptop Ultra) since Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is making an appearance. Microsoft is also streaming the event live from the Windows YouTube channel, with the title promising "something new," so we're sure to get insights on what's next for the world's most popular operating system. Finally, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been teasing Copilot as an OS following its recent redesign , which all but confirms that the AI chatbot will play a prominent role.
The event will start on Wednesday, Oct. 7, at 10 a.m. PT (1 p.m. EST). We expect to attend follow-up sessions and demos throughout the day after the presentation.
Microsoft is hosting the event at a private conference venue in San Francisco, Calif. Earlier this year, Microsoft held its Build developer conference at the Fort Mason Center , also in San Francisco.
The main presentation will take place on Oct. 7 at 10 a.m. PT (1 p.m. EST) and is slated to last an hour. You can watch the livestream from the Windows YouTube channel .

articles.title_orig: Trump floats firing top political advisers after report they helped a pro-Russian government
articles.title_zh: Trump floats firing top political advisers after report they helped a pro-Russian government
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump on Wednesday distanced himself from two of his top political advisers — less than 30 days before the midterm elections — writing that if their outside work presents a conflict, “I will terminate them, immediately!”
Trump’s warning came after The New York Times published a report detailing how James Blair, one of the president’s former deputy chiefs of staff who now leads his outside political operation, and Chris LaCivita, Trump’s 2024 co-campaign manager, traveled to the Balkans last week for paid work on behalf of a pro-Russian government.
Trump was unaware that the two men had traveled to the Balkans – or that the pro-Russian government was among their clientele – until he was briefed on the impending New York Times piece, sources familiar with the situation told CNN. The president then made a series of phone calls Tuesday night asking his allies what their take on the story was, the sources said.
One source said Trump appeared annoyed, and another veteran Republican who is in touch with the president told CNN that Trump was “pissed” by the report – particularly at the revelation that the two advisers had been abroad in the home stretch of the midterm campaign, profiting off their association with him.
“Tone deaf,” the veteran Republican said of the advisers’ conduct.
But another source said Trump was simply seeking a range of opinions on what had been reported.
Trump – who has been actively campaigning for Republicans ahead of November’s midterms – ultimately decided he wanted to respond to the story, two of the sources told CNN. So on Wednesday, one of the sources said, he dictated a Truth Social post to aide Natalie Harp while in the Oval Office, commenting to those in the room that both Blair and LaCivita are outside consultants and are allowed to have other clients. One source said that at that moment, he did not seem irked.
“Chris LaCivita and James Blair are outside consultants. They do not work for me, other than as outside consultants. They most likely have numerous clients, but for that, you would have to ask them,” Trump posted.
“I do not have any idea who else they work for but will, on reflection, ask them and, if there’s a conflict, I will terminate them, immediately!” Trump wrote.
The president continued distancing himself from the two advisers and downplayed any conflict of interest later Wednesday. “They don’t have a conflict because they’re independent people,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.
“I assume they have a lot of clients,” he went on. “So I don’t know their contract. If I thought they had a conflict … I would terminate.”
He also noted that neither currently works in the White House.
“Well they’re allowed to do that,” Trump told CNN. “They have a lot of clients and it’s okay. I’m a client over there, they have a consulting firm I guess, separately, as all people in Washington do. That’s pretty common.”
According to the Times, Blair and LaCivita traveled to Republika Srpska, a territory in Bosnia and Herzegovina, ahead of elections there on Sunday. The trip came as polls show Republicans are facing severe electoral challenges in the United States.
Blair and LaCivita “were paid hundreds of thousands of dollars each through a Washington-based law firm that was retained by Republika Srpska’s government to provide counsel on voting issues,” the Times reported.
They said the work was for the government and not the nationalist party that controls it, though they are essentially one and the same.
Blair currently leads Trump’s super PAC, MAGA Inc., and has been tasked with heading up the president’s midterm elections strategy. LaCivita is a senior adviser at MAGA Inc.
The group has been spending tens of millions of dollars trying to bolster Republican candidates ahead of the midterms, including some in reliably red territory who now appear vulnerable.
This story has been updated with additional developments.
CNN’s Kevin Liptak contributed to this report.

Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and U.S. President Donald Trump are seen in this combination of pictures created on Dec. 2, 2025.
President Donald Trump on Thursday said he is following the upcoming Brazilian election “very closely,” referring to Brazil as a “very important" country. "The people of Brazil are fantastic people,” he told reporters outside the White House. “It’s a very important election.”
The U.S. State Department later announced the suspension of its consular services in Brazil ahead of the election taking place on Sunday, citing unspecified security concerns. “U.S. citizens seeking emergency assistance during this time should not come to the Embassy, the Consulates, or other U.S. diplomatic facilities,” the security alert advised.
Brazilians are heading to the polls for a set of federal elections spanning congressional and gubernatorial races, alongside the first round of the presidential election votes. It’s set to be a decisive moment for Latin America’s largest nation, as the region has seen a shift toward the right in recent years. An Oct. 25 runoff is expected, as polls show a tight contest between leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and far-right Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro , who was convicted last year for plotting a coup to overturn his 2022 election loss. Trump led the conservative voices denouncing the conviction, referring to the trial as a “ witch hunt .”
While Trump has acknowledged his active interest as Brazil votes on its political future, there are concerns he could be too involved. Trump and his Administration have been accused of attempting to interfere with the high-stakes overseas election.
In a letter sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio in late September, Democratic lawmakers expressed “grave concern” over what they referred to as “the Administration’s coordinated effort to threaten our strategic alliance with Brazil and undermine the Western Hemisphere’s second-largest democracy ahead of its upcoming presidential election.”
“Over the course of President Trump’s second term, we have seen U.S. officials engage in a sustained, multifaceted campaign of interference and destabilization in Brazil,” the lawmakers said in the Sept. 24 letter, signed by 30 House Democrats and Independent Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont, who caucuses with the Democratic Party.
In another letter sent to Rubio on Monday, three Democratic Senators voiced similar concerns about potential U.S. interference.
“This effort first escalated sharply during the summer of 2025, with the [U.S.] Administration deploying tariffs and targeted sanctions to attempt to shape the Brazilian Supreme Court’s verdict in the trial of former President Jair Bolsonaro on charges of attempting to foment a military coup to stay in power,” said the Senators, noting that the tariff pressure escalated in July this year when the Trump Administration moved to impose a new 25% tariff on many imports from Brazil—a decision labeled a “lamentable milestone” by Lula’s office.
The Senators argued that the “campaign directed at Brazil’s authorities resumed with the appointment of Darren Beattie as a senior advisor on Brazil issues in the State Department.” Beattie served as a White House speech writer in Trump’s first term, but was axed for attending a gathering of white supremacists. He returned to the fold early on in Trump’s second term. When serving as undersecretary for public diplomacy and public affairs last year, he called one of Brazil’s Supreme Court Judges a “key architect of the censorship and persecution complex directed against Bolsonaro and his supporters.”
Accusing the Trump Administration of using “diplomatic, economic, and political pressure in ways that risk weakening [Brazil’s] democratic institutions [and] undermining confidence in Brazil's electoral process,” the Senators closed the letter by asking the Administration to “commit to recognizing the certified outcome of Brazil's 2026 democratic elections.”
The White House has staunchly rejected claims of interference in Brazil’s elections.
“Conservative leaders are winning elections across the Western Hemisphere on their own merit because everyone sees the success of President Trump’s policies,” said White House spokesperson Anna Kelly in a statement to TIME. “These claims are nonsense.”
President Lula has also expressed concern over Trump’s interest in his country’s election. “I have already told President Trump it is very important that the U.S. do not interfere in Brazil’s elections,” he said in a Sept. 22 interview. “Brazilian elections are the concern of the Brazilian people. American elections are the concern of the American people.”
Lula added that he is “very worried about Marco Rubio,” claiming that the U.S. Secretary of State “is very closely connected to Bolsonaro’s people,” though he stressed that this was only “suspicion.” TIME has reached out to the State Department for comment.
Trump has not formally endorsed either candidate in Brazil’s presidential race, but his defense of former Brazilian President Bolsonaro, who was last year sentenced to 27 years in prison, is well documented.
After Trump criticized the trial proceedings as a “terrible thing” in July 2025, the Trump Administration increased pressure on Brazil’s government by imposing punishing 50% tariffs— extended in part due to Bolsonaro’s treatment in the courts—and directing the office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) to investigate trade relations with the country.
The State Department added to the pressure later that same month, when Rubio called Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes’ actions a “political witch hunt against Jair Bolsonaro” and announced visa restrictions on Moraes, unspecified judicial allies, and their immediate families.
Feliciano de Sá Guimarães, an associate professor at the Institute of International Relations at the University of São Paulo, says Lula was able to turn the economic pressure into a political argument of his own.
“Lula realized that he could play [these threats] in his favor for electoral purposes,” he says, explaining that Lula used the concept of “ rally round the flag ,” meaning that once a country is targeted by another, “the incumbent President can rally the people and say, ‘look our sovereignty is under attack.’”
The theme of sovereignty has featured prominently in Lula’s 2026 government manifesto , which points to Trump’s tariffs as damaging the Brazilian economy.
Guimarães says the U.S. Administration has since slightly altered its strategy, favoring an approach that could instead benefit Lula’s opposition.
Flávio Bolsonaro met with Trump, Rubio, and Vice President J.D. Vance at the White House in May. Trump later described the Brazilian lawmaker as a “smart young man, who loves his country very much.” Shortly after that meeting, the U.S. Administration on May 28 designated Primeiro Comando da Capital and Comando Vermelho—two Brazilian gangs—as terrorist organizations, with Bolsonaro appearing to take credit for the move in the media.
Guimarães says the issue may have resonated in Brazil due to public concerns about crime.
“Brazilians are so desperate with the situation of crime in the country that they are resorting to support any initiative, whether it's coming from the federal government or a foreign power to fix the problem,” Guimarães explains, so the move could be seen to strengthen Bolsonaro’s chances with the electorate.
Economic pressure has continued as well. After ordering the USTR to investigate Brazil’s trade practices last year, the office imposed 25% tariffs on the country in July under Section 301, for what it described as unfair trade practices.
Other disputes have further heightened diplomatic tensions. At the end of July, Brazil denied visas to two U.S. State Department officials, accusing them of trying to interfere in the upcoming election. Shortly afterward, Brazilian Ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeir

articles.title_orig: The World Has Risen for Palestine. Houston Must Rise Too.
articles.title_zh: The World Has Risen for Palestine. Houston Must Rise Too.
articles.content_orig:
This piece was originally published at Shift Press , a youth-centered publication that provides news and journalism training, encouraging Houston youth toward civic engagement.
On July 4, 2025, the people of Gaza experienced another round of relentless hellfire from occupation fighter jets. In just 24 hours, Israel murdered 138 Palestinians , half of whom were killed waiting for food and water under the U.S./Israeli-induced famine. Massacres like this are not unfamiliar to the Palestinian people, nor the movement supporting them. Neither is the grief that accompanies such atrocities, too large to be contained to Gaza's 365 square kilometers. It is a kind of grief and anger that cannot be summed up by memoirs or homage. It is one that requires political reckoning and, most importantly, intervention. As we witnessed the inaction from our local government, we knew that this intervention would have to come from us, the people of Houston.
That same July 4, weathering Houston's 100-degree summer heat, a group of organizers climbed the hills of Eleanor Tinsley Park. Weaving through blankets, lawn chairs, and families staking out spots for Houston's annual fireworks show, we distributed hundreds of flyers on the role this city played in facilitating the genocide in Gaza. We closed the day with the unfurling of a banner which read: "THE U.S. AND ISRAEL ARE STARVING GAZA." We weren't sure what to expect. The slow erasure of Palestine from the news cycle would make us believe that people had become apathetic, even antagonistic, to our cause. To our surprise, we were met with 'Free, Free Palestine' chants so loud that they broke through the noise of the fireworks show.
In that moment we learned that Houstonians were ready for something different. That our city, whose streets once carried the weight of 25,000+ people marching in unison for Gaza, was far ahead of the local political elite on the question of Palestinian liberation. This small, powerful moment last July became the genesis of the Houston Arms Embargo campaign.
In 2024, the Palestinian Youth Movement's Mask Off Maersk campaign published a groundbreaking report documenting the central role of Maersk, the world's second largest container shipping line, in transporting components for Israel's F-35 fighter jet. The F-35, known as the 'crown jewel' of the Israeli military, has been used by Israel to carry out countless massacres across Gaza, most infamously the 2024 al-Mawasi camp massacre in which Israel murdered at least 90 Palestinians. In order for this devastating military cargo to reach the clutches of the IDF, it must first pass through Houston. From 2020 to 2025, 432 shipments of F-35 fighter jet parts passed through the Port of Houston, to be assembled into jets in Fort Worth's Lockheed Martin facility and flown to Israel. The Port of Houston has facilitated more shipments of F-35 fighter jet wings than any other port in the United States.
After learning the full extent of the port's complicity in Israel's war crimes, the Palestinian Youth Movement and Palestine Solidarity TX began making expeditions to the Port of Houston. We met with dockworkers, learned about Maersk's treatment of laborers, and coordinated flyer drops and letter deliveries to Maersk's Houston office. This work was instrumental in mounting international pressure against the shipping giant.
At the same time, we witnessed a shift within the international movement for Palestine towards local campaigns for an arms embargo. From workers in Italy and Spain leading national work stoppages to prevent shipment of military cargo through their ports, to the launch of the Oakland People's Arms Embargo by the Bay Area chapter of the Palestinian Youth Movement, we knew that it was time to localize our demand for Maersk and challenge the use of Houston's public infrastructure for genocide.
The shift to organizing an arms embargo campaign in Houston was rooted in a few developments in the struggle: 1) the genocide on Gaza raged on with more ferocity and international impunity than anyone had imagined 2) we recognized that a vast majority of Houstonians were on the side of the Palestinians and wanted an immediate end to the slaughter and 3) local pro-Israel politicians like John Whitmire and the city council members who backed him were facing rapid political isolation and unpopularity in the city.
We launched the Houston Arms Embargo not only because of the moral righteousness of our demands. The local context of Houston had become increasingly favorable to coalition-building for Palestine. We recognized that we could take the widespread anger and grief Houstonians felt watching the genocide unfold and turn it into something with political teeth. Our campaign has been dedicated to building tangible, grassroots power to leverage towards our singular demand: end the transport of military cargo through the Port of Houston.
Since launching last summer, the Houston Arms Embargo campaign has built a coalition of more than 40 community and advocacy organizations. Organizers have collected over 4,000 signatures, testified at Port Houston Port Authority meetings, hosted public events, and organized demonstrations at Barbours Cut Terminal, where ships carrying F-35 components arrive every month. We're building power through organized labor, through advocacy and outreach, and creating a network of institutions and individuals who can, through their unity in action, inflict real political costs for the port's continued facilitation of genocide cargo.
The Houston Arms Embargo is one of the few campaigns that has been able to sustain a galvanized, activated base. While this can be attributed in no small part to the diligent organizing of the campaign, we believe its success is rooted in something far more intrinsic: the people of Houston crave political leadership. For two years, elected officials across our city and state did everything in their power to avoid the question of Palestine. Many could not even muster up a meager "thought and prayer" in the face of Palestinian bodies piling up under the rubble of their homes. If the last two years have taught our city anything, it's that leadership is not a title or a paycheck. It is having the courage to understand the needs of working-class Houstonians and prioritize them over the interests of donors and lobbying groups. And when our city government could not, our campaign could. For that, Houstonians continue to join our campaign with enthusiasm, conviction, and dedication.
The reality in Gaza is bleak. Daily bombing campaigns rage on while Trump's so-called "Board of Peace" seeks to concentrate groups of Palestinians into "humanitarian safe-zones," a thin veil for the codification of Israel's illegal occupation of Gaza. The Palestinian people deserve justice. They deserve to live in peace in their homeland. A single hair on the head of a maimed Palestinian child is as heavy as the U.S.-made bomb used to kill him. And no political jargon is strong enough to convince the people of Houston to accept our city's infrastructure being used for the bombing of another church, or mosque, or hospital, or school, or safe zone, or aid distribution site, or UN office, or cafe, or soccer game. We know that this struggle will be long, but times are changing, and with each protest, demonstration, and initiative made by our campaign, we get closer to a free Palestine and a better, more just world for all who inhabit it.
This is the Houston Arms Embargo. Join our fight today.
Sign the petition to demand an end to the use of Houston's infrastructure for genocide here . To learn more about the Houston Arms Embargo campaign and upcoming events, visit its website and Instagram .
The Houston Arms Embargo campaign is building a citywide movement to shut down this supply chain of death. The people of Houston refuse to be complicit in genocide and are uniting under one clear demand: No More Military Cargo for Israel through the Port

articles.title_orig: Merz’s conservatives in new crisis over alleged support for AfD
articles.title_zh: Merz’s conservatives in new crisis over alleged support for AfD
articles.content_orig:
A normally ho-hum procedural vote in a small state was closely watched across Germany on Tuesday, when a far-right politician was elected to lead a state legislature for the first time since the Nazi era.
In the legislative election last month in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, the Alternative for Germany party, labeled “suspected extremist” by Germany’s domestic intelligence service, won 39 of 83 seats. The party, known by its German initials AfD, far outperformed every other party, delivering a shock to the country’s postwar consensus.
The next step toward taking power occurred on Tuesday, when lawmakers were sworn in and elected the AfD’s Tobias Rausch as president of the Parliament. In that role, Mr. Rausch, 35, will preside over the legislative agenda, parliamentary bureaucracy and ceremonial roles, like hosting memorials commemorating the Holocaust.
In the anonymous vote, 48 lawmakers voted for Mr. Rausch, meaning that he received the support of some members of mainstream parties that have officially refused to work with the AfD.
A higher, more important hurdle awaits in December, when the state Parliament is expected to fill the most powerful state position, minister president — the equivalent of governor, with control of the executive branch. It is unclear if the AfD’s candidate, Ulrich Siegmund , can win that vote; until then Sven Schulze of the Christian Democrats remains acting governor of Saxony-Anhalt, one of Germany’s least populous states, with about 2.1 million people.
The party has made it clear that it does not intend to allow business as usual.
The AfD successfully ran on an anti-immigration, anti-establishment campaign, pro-fossil fuel campaign, but such issues are decided on the federal level, beyond the reach of a state government. At the state level, it plans to focus on education and culture issues.

articles.title_orig: Nissan UK launches first ‘real-world’ driverless pilot
articles.title_zh: Nissan UK launches first ‘real-world’ driverless pilot
articles.content_orig:
Part of a government-funded research project that originated at the University of Warwick, it aims to deploy an autonomous mobility service across the U.K.
Nissan U.K.’s business unit will bring autonomous driving services to the university city of Cambridge and test its latest technology in an urban enviorment and create a blueprint to launch in other communities.
The plans are part of a government-funded research project backed by Nissan that launched in September 2023 at the University of Warwick with the goal of deploying an autonomous mobility service across the U.K.
The pilot trial, dubbed “ADventure,” will be coordinated between the automaker, local authorities, commuters and residents, the company said in its Sept. 28 release .
Using a specially adapted 2022 Nissan Leaf electric vehicle , the project hopes to focus on how future AD technology “can create social value, improve accessibility and address local transport challenges,” Nissan said.
The automaker used the common example of elderly people in the U.K. having to travel to a medical appointment when they do not drive themselves.
Nissan will draw on more than a decade of research by its engineers at the Nissan Technical Center Europe, which will lead the autonomous mobility project.
By choosing the driving environment in Cambridge for the automaker’s first real-world trial, Nissan aims to create a blueprint that it can refine and replicate across the U.K.
“This project is an important step for autonomous mobility in the UK,” said David Moss, SVP research and development for Nissan vehicles across the Africa, Middle East, India, Europe and Oceania regions. “With UK Government backing, it will take autonomous vehicle research beyond central London and into another city, helping us understand how these services can work for different communities and real-life journeys.”
“By developing and applying Nissan’s in-house expertise, combined with the wider knowledge from our partners, we can delve further into how self-driving vehicles can improve connectivity, accessibility and quality of everyday life,” Moss added.

articles.title_orig: Kirby Smart addresses Isaias hurricane threat, Georgia preparation
articles.title_zh: Kirby Smart addresses Isaias hurricane threat, Georgia preparation
articles.content_orig:
ATHENS — Georgia coach Kirby Smart is keeping his focus on the Alabama game — not the weather — as Saturday’s showdown in Tuscaloosa approaches.
Tropical Storm Isaias is heading toward the gulf coast, and WALA-Mobile is reporting it is forecast to strengthen to a hurricane on Thursday.
The National Hurricane Center is forecasting the system to turn toward the north on Friday and has projections indicating the path of the storm might reach Tuscaloosa.
Georgia is scheduled to play at Alabama in Bryant-Denny Stadium at 7:30 p.m. on Saturday.
“It’s certainly beyond my control, so we as coaches game plan for multiple situations for weather conditions when they’re there,” Smart said. “We had the same prep last week with the threat of those things, so (it) doesn’t change a lot about practice.”
Heavy rains and wind were originally forecast for Georgia’s home game with Vanderbilt last Saturday, but the storms did not come to pass.
Smart said the same staples apply to each practice week.
“You still have good on good, you’ve got to practice for the long term of the season, not just one week,” Smart said. “You can’t really practice conditions, you can’t simulate them, so you’re much better to educate (and) learn from the past of other people that have played in them and prepare your team to play and not make it about that.”
Smart said he has and will continue to get updates on the projected weather.
“I’m focused on trying to prepare our team, and game plan, and scheme, and all of those things,” Smart said. “I have an update, and they keep m updated with what’s going on (with) meetings, decisions, the way things are leaning and things like that.”
Smart said he does not have any input on any decisions that might be made about the scheduling of the game, and he is not aware of any timeline associated with possible changes.

articles.title_orig: OpenAI says teens use ChatGPT for under 15 minutes a day as worries over risks grow
articles.title_zh: OpenAI says teens use ChatGPT for under 15 minutes a day as worries over risks grow
articles.content_orig:
OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens was designed to promote healthier use of the artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot, but new research has found its important safety features fall short.
The major AI firm rolled out many teen safety guardrails in August, including curbs on emotional dependence and new parental alerts for problematic use.
On Wednesday, OpenAI said it found average teen use of ChatGPT to be relatively limited and tended toward "learning" activity.
However, research released the same day from non-profit Common Sense Media found that ChatGPT still poses an "unacceptable risk" for teens as safety features, including notifying parents of self-harm conversations, often fail.
When OpenAI this summer released what it called ChatGPT for Teens , it said users identified as being between the ages of 13 and 17 would be opted into "features to promote healthy use and additional controls for parents".
Those features include preventing teen ChatGPT users from engaging in romantic or other language that could encourage " emotional dependence," including preventing the tool from implying that it was in any way conscious. There are also blocks on sexualized imagery and "reminders" for teens if they were to share an image that was "sensitive."
The features are also meant to enable parents to receive notifications, if they had linked to their children's ChatGPT account, about chats that included discussions of self-harm or disordered eating.
OpenAI said those features have caused an uptick in teen use focused on learning, from study help to advice on their school work.
In addition to seeing the average teen user on ChatGPT for less than 15 minutes a day, OpenAI said that for longer stretches of use, automatic reminders to take a break work well. Almost half of teen users quickly stopped using ChatGPT after such a reminder.
The company added that, for teens who are seen to have used ChatGPT for three consecutive hours or more, their prompts included something related to learning in more than 80% of such cases.
But Common Sense Media's new research determined that ChatGPT for Teens was an "unacceptable risk" for young people and parents, and said OpenAI should ban people under 18 years old from using the platform until teen guardrails were proven reliable.
An OpenAI spokesman said a review of Common Sense Media's methodology found that much of the testing may have begun and concluded before activation of parental controls was complete."
"We welcome rigorous independent evaluation, but we do not believe Common Sense Media's testing accurately reflects how ChatGPT's teen safeguards work in practice or expert perspectives on how AI can support teens," he said.
While the firm's research, done through multiple accounts registered as belonging to a teen and conversations before and after the teen guardrails were put in place, found that ChatGPT was good at avoiding "sexual roleplay" with young users, other OpenAI guardrails failed, including for discussions of suicide.
The research found that even an hour of teen-ChatGPT conversation about "suicidal ideation, self-harm, or disordered eating on newly created, parent-linked accounts" resulted in "zero" alerts sent to parents.
It was only older ChatGPT accounts with "weeks of accumulated conversation history on sensitive topics" that would result in a parental alert.
In such conversations, ChatGPT also "failed to reliably recommend that teens in crisis connect to a hotline or professional," the report found.
The tests also showed that ChatGPT for Teens continues to do school work, and that the bot still will engage in anthropomorphised language or "talk like it's a friend," despite OpenAI's promise to curb that behaviour.
"ChatGPT for Teens could give parents false confidence in guardrails and safety alerts that frequently don't work," Tom Siegel, who leads the Youth AI Safety Institute within Common Sense, said.
The way young people interact with online platforms has become a major issue in recent years as self-harm and suicide among children has become more common.
This year has seen several lawsuits looking to hold companies like Meta , TikTok and others responsible for harming the mental health of children end in unprecedented losses for the firms.
OpenAI, too, has come under increased scrutiny and legal pressure over the way young people use ChatGPT.
The Tumbler Ridge mass shooting in rural Canada in February was carried out by an 18-year old who had for months prior been discussing gun violence with ChatGPT.
OpenAI has previously apologised for failing to flag the shooter's account with law enforcement, and is facing several lawsuits over the incident.

articles.title_orig: Trump claims world’s lowest drug prices. TrumpRx discounts are a ‘mixed bag,’ report shows.
articles.title_zh: Trump claims world’s lowest drug prices. TrumpRx discounts are a ‘mixed bag,’ report shows.
articles.content_orig:
Ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, President Donald Trump has increasingly touted his drug pricing deals, claiming the U.S. is now paying the world’s lowest prescription drug prices. “This one thing alone should win us the midterms,” he recently said at the White House.
TrumpRx.gov, the public face of his drug pricing discounts, has grown dramatically since its launch in February. What started as a few dozen brand-name drugs now includes a catalog of more than 800 brand-name and generic medications, offering discounts on everything from popular weight loss drugs to treatments for cancer and rheumatoid arthritis.
It’s unclear whether the average American has “ saved a fortune,” as Trump promised .
Prescription drug prices fell by 3.1% over the year ending in July, according to federal inflation data — though experts say it’s too soon to know how much of the drop, if any, can be attributed to Trump’s drug pricing deals. The site has relied on GoodRx’s pricing data and technology to power many of its listings and blends pre-existing discounts from drugmakers with newly negotiated prices.
At the Republican midterm convention last month , Trump said, “We went from the highest prescription drug prices, by far, anywhere in the world, to the lowest prescription drug prices anywhere in the world.”
A recent analysis from KFF finds that TrumpRx prices are competitive with prices in other countries for a small number of cancer and cholesterol medications. In many cases, Americans aren’t getting the best deals compared with the rest of the world.
Take Ozempic. For the average patient in the U.S. paying out of pocket, the blockbuster diabetes drug can cost $349 to more than $1,000 a month. It’s $349 through TrumpRx. Yet in several other wealthy countries, the next-highest price is $190 a month, according to KFF, a nonpartisan research group.
Enbrel is an even starker example. A monthly supply of the rheumatoid arthritis drug costs $3,354 through TrumpRx, more than five times the $641 average in the other countries where researchers found prices.
Some drugs, however, come out well ahead. Rydapt, a drug used to treat certain blood cancers, costs $2,909 for 56 capsules through TrumpRx — less than half the $5,901 price for the same amount in France, the next-cheapest country.
Those disparities run throughout the site, according to the KFF analysis. The report, which didn’t compare TrumpRx savings within the U.S., offers one of the first broad worldwide comparisons of Trump’s drug pricing claims.
The analysis looked at 32 brand-name drugs sold through TrumpRx that lacked generic or biosimilar equivalents. Researchers focused on those drugs because patients don’t have the option of switching to cheaper versions, meaning the discounts offered through TrumpRx could have a greater impact on what they pay.
The group compared the prices with those in 11 other wealthy countries, including Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom. The prices are current as of Aug. 26.
The results were almost evenly split. For 17 of the drugs, the TrumpRx prices were lower than the average prices abroad. For 15, they were higher. But Trump has promised Americans the lowest prices in the world. By that measure, the results were less favorable: Only five were actually the lowest-priced, while 13 were the highest-priced.
“It’s kind of a mixed bag,” said Juliette Cubanski, deputy director of the Medicare policy program at KFF, who co-authored the report. “Even with the reductions that may have been agreed to by manufacturers who are listing their drugs on the TrumpRx website, the prices that they’re offering, even at a discount, still continue to be higher than prices in comparable countries.”
The findings offer an early look at both the promise and the limits of Trump’s approach to lowering drug prices.
Americans routinely pay more for prescription drugs than patients in other wealthy countries, even when the medications are made by the same companies. The TrumpRx discounts, the White House says, stem from Trump’s “ most favored nation ” pricing deals, agreements with drugmakers to charge Americans the lower prices they offer other countries in exchange for tariff relief. But the discounts can vary widely, the analysis found, and they haven’t consistently produced the lowest prices Trump promised.
“I’m not surprised by these findings,” said Dr. Benjamin Rome, a primary care physician and health policy researcher at Harvard Medical School. “Any of us who have been following drug prices realized, as soon as TrumpRx was launched, it was a limited number of drugs and it was clear that the prices that were there were not always going to be linked or in any way related to what the prices are in other countries.”
It’s a markedly different approach from the one taken by Trump’s predecessor Joe Biden.
Rather than use Medicare’s power to negotiate prices for a limited number of costly drugs each year, TrumpRx relies largely on voluntary agreements with individual drugmakers to offer discounted prices directly to consumers. (The exact details of the agreements remain largely confidential, and the White House has declined to disclose them.)
TrumpRx doesn’t sell the drugs directly. For many drugs, it sends consumers to manufacturer programs through which they can obtain coupons or discounted cash prices without insurance.
That’s not how most people get their prescription drugs. About 9 in 10 Americans have some form of health insurance , meaning many pay for medications through private insurance, Medicare or Medicaid — although discounted cash-pay options have become increasingly popular as insurance has gotten more expensive. The money spent on TrumpRx doesn’t count toward a patient’s copay or deductible.
“They’re highly selected products where the manufacturer is willing to offer a discount,” Rome said. “Maybe they’re not the products causing the highest spending in the U.S. in some cases or are products where they were already offering confidential discounts, but now they’re making those discounts more public.”
The site now includes several cheaper, generic medications. “But those generics and the low prices for those generics pre-existed the TrumpRx website ,” Cubanski said.
The KFF analysis doesn’t capture every drug available through TrumpRx, and there are limits to how much can be concluded from it.
Antonio Ciaccia, CEO of 46brooklyn Research, a group that tracks drug pricing in the U.S., counts about 80 brand-name drugs currently on TrumpRx, while KFF was able to compare prices for 32.
Part of the challenge, Ciaccia said, is that some drugs sold in the U.S. aren’t available in all of the countries KFF examined. That can make direct comparisons difficult.
“One of the big differences is the U.S. market does have more products in it than international markets, so that is noteworthy to the extent we have options here in the U.S. rather than a one-size-fits-all treatment approach,” he said.
International prices aren’t always perfectly comparable, either, he said. The analysis relied on publicly available prices, which may not include confidential discounts negotiated between foreign governments and drugmakers.
Ciaccia also noted that KFF’s 11 comparison countries don’t exactly match the countries used in some of the administration’s international pricing programs.
A White House spokesperson referred NBC News to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services for comment. The CMS didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
Those limitations don’t change the basic comparison at the heart of Trump’s claim: whether the prices offered to Americans match or beat those available abroad.
“We wanted to put that claim to the test with this analysis,” Cubanski said. “There is not a clear pattern across the board for higher prices or no consistent pattern across the board for lower prices. ”
And the administration has increasingly made broader claims that it has accomplished just that

articles.title_orig: Trump seems pretty sore over Republicans not wanting to campaign with him
articles.title_zh: Trump seems pretty sore over Republicans not wanting to campaign with him
articles.content_orig:
It has become abundantly clear that Republicans in tough races aren’t especially eager to campaign with President Donald Trump ahead of the midterm election.
Few of them showed up to Trump’s midterm convention last month. His travel schedule since then has rather curiously featured lower-tier states like Alabama, Oklahoma and New York and only a handful of real battleground races. And even in Texas, Gov. Greg Abbott is skipping Trump’s upcoming rally (citing scheduling conflicts, of course).
Trump increasingly appears rather sensitive about this dynamic — which makes sense, given he’s latched onto the theory that he alone can push his party to victory in less than four weeks, despite his low approval numbers.
He went on a tear about his rallies on Tuesday, bringing it up at least five separate times.
“By the way, I’m going around doing rallies. The Republican Party is starting to go right through the roof,” he said at a non-campaign event in Baltimore. “Somebody said today, ‘I wonder why?’ Well, I started — I had to get out. I had to do it.”
(There is no evidence Trump’s rallies are actually helping, which we’ll get to.)
He posted on social media that his “Rally crowds and enthusiasm are unbelievable!” He added: “ We are flipping races all over the place . … It’s all happening!”
In a separate post, he said simply: “ MY RALLIES ARE SAVING THE REPUBLICAN PARTY, AGAIN!!! ”
In gaggles with reporters, he returned to the topic even when he wasn’t asked about it, claiming at one point that “the rallies have changed things around.” When asked about leaked audio of Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton saying DC was controlling his campaign, Trump responded that Paxton was “doing much better” since Trump started doing rallies a few days ago.
And when a reporter asked Monday about campaigning in Michigan, Trump said he would. When asked about campaigning in Maine, he suggested he would go there, too.
“I don’t know about Maine,” Trump said. “I think we’re going to Maine, too.”
But GOP Sen. Susan Collins has said repeatedly — including at a debate Tuesday night — that she didn’t expect Trump to come to Maine. “That’s just not going to happen,” Collins said in June .
This is also an uneasy question in Iowa, where three House Republicans recently broke from Trump somewhat on the Iran war. And Senate candidate Rep. Ashley Hinson seems to want some distance from Trump.
When those lawmakers were at a White House event last week, Trump seemed to put them on the spot, bringing up plans for more campaign events with him.
“I’m going to come to Iowa,” Trump said, adding: “I will say that we’re going to do a great rally, and we’ll all be there together. We have to get you all elected.”
Hinson responded: “We’ll save you a good Iowa pork chop, sir.”
And back in early September, when it became clear many Republicans in marquee races were skipping the president’s Trump-centric midterm convention, the president claimed it was for reasons beside his historically low poll numbers.
“Everybody wants to come,” Trump maintained, adding: “The reason that some people are not coming is because we don’t have room for 500 politicians.”
He also said back then that he would be all over the country, campaigning for every Republican in the most competitive races.
“I’m going to go to every one of those 35 places, and we’re going to see if we can get everyone elected,” he said September 2. He repeated the same claim at the convention a week later: “I’m gonna go to every one of them, about 35. In a couple of cases, I’ll go twice.”
That doesn’t appear to be happening anymore — at least not yet. With less than four weeks to go, Trump has been to only a handful of true battleground areas.
And despite Trump’s claim that he’s such an asset, it appears that his “Trump-a-palooza” midterm convention backfired on Republicans. Polls show the generic ballot, a key measure of the midterm, took a turn in Democrats’ favor at almost that precise moment.
Of course, Trump simply can’t allow for this perception that Republicans don’t want to campaign with him and that he’s an electoral burden.
His ability to rally the base at raucous, large-scale events has been a central part of his political brand, yet he’s confronting a reality where many Republicans seem to view them as net-negatives.
The lack of Republicans pining to campaign with him also calls into question his domination of his party, which he has been cultivating for a decade and is central to his hold on what political capital he has left. If he truly lost the base and his ability to make Republicans do what he wants, he wouldn’t have much left.
In the four-week span left before the election, it could become abundantly clear just how many Republicans think Trump is an albatross and a lame duck.
So he’s over-compensating for that — badly.

articles.title_zh: We now have images of the smart home products that Apple and LG are reportedly cooking up
articles.content_orig:
These include a lock, a thermostat and a temperature sensor.
A recent report indicated that Apple and LG have teamed up to develop several smart home gadgets, with an official reveal expected next week . Now, a reputable leaker has posted several renders of these gadgets, along with some specifications.
These leaked images feature the smart lock, thermostat and temperature sensor. The LG Smart Deadbolt Lock looks to have a keypad that rotates to open. It reportedly supports automatic unlocking and tap to unlock, with integrated emergency power and master codes. The leaker says it ships with two mechanical keys.
Here's your first look at home accessories Apple has co-developed with LG. 🧵
• The keypad rotates to open. You can use the included swivel pin to limit the rotation on one side so it doesn't touch a wall. • Settings for Touchpad Light Ring, Door... pic.twitter.com/Gy8CFXvc1F
— pdfu (@itspdfu) October 7, 2026
The LG Smart Thermostat includes settings for humidity, brightness and language. As for the design, it looks pretty much like every other smart thermostat out there. It's circular and, you know, thermostat-shaped.
The LG Temperature Sensor can also sense humidity and features a magnetic back for attaching to metal surfaces. It ships with a replaceable battery.
• Temperature and humidity sensing. • The sensor has a magnetic back to attach to metal surfaces. Comes with a metal plate with adhesive for attaching to other surfaces. • Replaceable battery and replacement alerts. pic.twitter.com/MCsBbtiBie
— pdfu (@itspdfu) October 7, 2026
These aren't the only three smart home devices that the two companies are likely cooking up. Reporting suggests that Apple and LG are also working on a video doorbell, an indoor camera, an outdoor camera and a floodlight camera. All of these gadgets will reportedly launch under the LG branding, and not as Apple products.

articles.title_orig: Exclusive | Wells Fargo Faces Regulator Probe Over Efforts to Boost Black Homeownership
articles.title_zh: Exclusive | Wells Fargo Faces Regulator Probe Over Efforts to Boost Black Homeownership
articles.content_orig:
The Department of Housing and Urban Development is examining whether the bank's programs aimed at helping minority homebuyers violated federal fair-housing laws.
The Trump Administration is looking to investigate Wells Fargo regarding programs and commitments the longtime bank has made to increase homeownership for Black Americans .
Per a report from the Wall Street Journal , the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) sent Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf a letter stating that it would examine whether the bank violated fair-lending laws in its programs to assist potential minority homeowners. Per HUD, it could be considered a violation of the Fair Housing Act.
"Even if Wells Fargo did not violate the law, its practice of dividing Americans based on race is immoral, unethical and un-American," HUD Secretary Scott Turner wrote. "Wells Fargo and all of its employees that engaged in race-based decision-making should be ashamed of themselves."
In 2017, during the first Trump Administration, Wells Fargo announced a commitment to lend $60 billion to help at least 250,000 African American homeowners by 2027. Five years following that announcement, the bank expanded the program to put the company's own money to work refinancing minority homes.
"These efforts are an important next step and will help close the homeownership gap between white and minority families created by decades of systemic inequities," Wells Fargo said in 2022.
Despite Wells Fargo scaling down its mortgage business in 2023 and removing its diversity, equity and inclusion references shortly after Trump took office in January 2025, HUD states the company's obligations "rise or fall based on actual practices, not buzzwords or website aesthetics."
The effort is part of a widespread attempt by the administration to curtail all diversity, equity and inclusion programs , from federal and local governments to colleges, businesses and more.
Housing statistics continue to remain low regarding Black homeowners compared to their white, Asian and Hispanic counterparts. According to LendingTree , only 43.6% of Black households owned the homes they lived in, compared with 70.1% of white households. Atlanta has the highest population of Black households who own the home they live in at 55%, followed by Birmingham, Alabama (54%) and Richmond, Virginia (52.8%).

articles.title_orig: World’s largest steam locomotive returns to the rails for special holiday tour
articles.title_zh: World’s largest steam locomotive returns to the rails for special holiday tour
articles.content_orig:
For the first time since 2019, Union Pacific’s Living Legend No. 844 will be hitting the rails with Big Boy No. 4014. These historic locomotives will be together for a special holiday tour this November.
On November 21, the pair of steam locomotives will run during a fundraising tour from Greeley to Denver, Colorado. The trip will benefit the Make-A-Wish Foundation, with a donation from Union Pacific’s Community Ties Giving Program. The steam duo will also be on display to the public at Denver’s Union Station. Santa Claus and his elves will even be in the terminal handing out limited-edition gifts. Admission to this event is free and open to the public.
Tickets for the holiday fundraising tour to take a ride in vintage passenger cars pulled by Big Boy and No. 844 go on sale to patrons of the Union Pacific Railroad Museum on October 16. The general public can purchase any remaining tickets on October 19. Families can still visit Denver’s Union Station to view the locomotives free of charge.
Nicknamed the “Living Legend,” No. 844 is a famed high-speed passenger locomotive . It was built in 1944 and the last steam locomotive built for Union Pacific. It hauled some of the company’s most recognizable passenger trains, including the Overland Limited, Los Angeles Limited, Portland Rose, and Challenger . No. 844 is also the last Class I North American steam locomotive and never permanently retired from service. Instead, it was reassigned to freight service in Nebraska from 1957 to 1959, when diesel locomotives took over passenger service duties. Unlike nearly every other steam locomotive of its era, No. 844 escaped the scrap yard in 1960 and Union Pacific retained it for special service.
No. 844 will chug alongside a more famous locomotive, Big Boy No. 4014. Big Boy is currently the world’s largest operating steam locomotive and one of only eight remaining Big Boys in existence and the only one still in operation. These powerful locomotives were constructed during World War II to transport heavy equipment to support the war effort.
Earlier this year, Big Boy drew millions of spectators during a coast-to-coast journey celebrating the United States’ 250th birthday . The first leg began on March 29. Big Boy then traveled to several states including California, Utah, and New York.
The steam locomotive celebrated the Fourth of July in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania , where the Declaration of Independence was written in 1776. Thousands of train enthusiasts braved temperatures of 102 degrees Fahrenheit (with a real-feel of 112 degrees) to catch a glimpse of the 133-foot-long and 1.2-million-pound train.

articles.title_orig: This Is Not an Anniversary
articles.title_zh: This Is Not an Anniversary
articles.content_orig:
Does remembering the date of October 7 make it easier to name?
A man carries away a Palestinian killed in an Israeli airstrike at the Erez crossing between Israel and the northern Gaza Strip, on October 7, 2023.
The world remembers Gaza again this week. Had Palestinians wanted remembrance after each date we experienced atrocity, a full, long year wouldn’t have enough days. We have been faithful victims, though, haven’t we? Since 2023, the world has applauded the resilience of our bare chests standing up to the tanks grinding us dead. Our blood must’ve shed beautifully. The women and children mourning everything and everyone they had ever known have cried in perfect tears for protests and, indeed, outraged slogans. Our homes, no longer recognizable, could have been spared if they had not borne witness to lifetimes of destruction. And if only our screams hadn’t been too loud. Three years in, forgive us for not making as many stories about our sons and daughters as the world can give standing ovations. I wish my late journalist colleagues were a bit more courageous to commit a crime and call it out. They would have been worthy of support. Probably they would’ve been deserving of protection.
My life has become a tale of a thousand anniversaries. So I dare ask: Does remembering the date of a tragedy make it easier to name? To live with? How is recalling our trauma—and dedicating an anniversary for it—going to help erase it? How is the mere reflection on something still happening and painful beyond any human’s language will bring it to an end? The notion of marking an anniversary that kicked off a rather inhumane and unimaginable memory in a long history of erasure points to the fact that the world has already moved on. It supposes that all we ever asked for was empathy. And that, frankly, is why we’re more at peace with a senseless world than we are with our tragedies. If the moral urge behind holding an anniversary is to hold space for the grief that the past few years have inflicted, by no means should this say that we’re past the grieving. If it was to end this grief, then we’re not even in any way close to doing so.
And although I’ve written constantly and with abundant detail about all the personal and collective agony I have endured over the last three years, I still haven’t been able to put into words the true feeling of realizing that with each anniversary of death we become one year closer to life. But here is what I am able to say.
A day on which entire bloodlines were erased from the civil registry should not be an anniversary.
A day our mothers were crushed beneath the concrete of their own kitchens should not be an anniversary.
A day newborns suffocated in dark, unpowered incubators should not be an anniversary.
A day flour sacks were soaked in the blood of men standing in line for bread should not be an anniversary.
A day children had their limbs amputated without anesthesia on blood-slicked hospital floors should not be an anniversary.
A day thousands of tons of explosives flattened every school, university, hospital, and library should not be an anniversary.
A day our grandparents were forced to relive their displacement under relentless bombardment should not be an anniversary.
A day white shroud shortages forced us to bury three generations in a single shallow trench should not be an anniversary.
A day parents carried what remained of their children in plastic bags should not be an anniversary.
A day entire cities were turned into a blinding wasteland of pulverized stone and bone should not be an anniversary.
A day refugee tents were set ablaze while families slept on the sand should not be an anniversary.
A day doctors, poets, teachers, civil defense crews, and journalists were targeted for bearing witness should not be an anniversary.
A day mothers dug through scorching rubble with bare hands until their fingernails ripped away should not be an anniversary.
A day drop-delivered aid crushed the starving people it was meant to feed should not be an anniversary.
A day human beings were hunted through ruined alleyways by silent quadcopters should not be an anniversary.
A day ancient olive groves, centuries-old mosques and churches, and family photo albums were bulldozed into dirt should not be an anniversary.
A day an entire generation was orphaned, maimed, and stripped of a future should not be an anniversary.
A day hundreds of infants starved to death while their mothers did not have enough formula to feed them should not be an anniversary.
A day the sky turned into a screaming engine of death overhead should not be an anniversary.
A day our memories, our songs, and our homes were buried under mountains of gray ash should not be an anniversary.
A day the global audience watched a live-streamed genocide and called it defense should not be an anniversary.
Do not attempt to mark a date on a calendar that is not yours. If you do, keep your prayers—or celebrations—and let us keep what remains of your dignity.
Mohammed Mhawish is a contributing writer for The Nation . He is a journalist originally from Gaza City and a contributor to the book A Land With a People . He has also written for + 972, Al Jazeera, MSNBC, The Economist , and more. Subscribe to his newsletter here .
